bib.title: Sparks of Artificial General Intelligence: Early experiments with GPT-4

read.skipped: Qualitative transcripts not read line by line: most of Section 3.2 and 3.1.2 code listings, 4.1 and 4.3-4.4 maths conversations, Section 5 (tool use, games), Section 6.1 theory of mind and 6.2 explainability dialogues, references, and Appendices A, B, C.2-C.6, D.2-D.4, E, F, G tables other than Table 10 tail. question: What can an early, pre-release, text-only version of GPT-4 do across many domains, and does it show signs of general intelligence?
hypothesis: GPT-4 (this early version) exhibits more general intelligence than previous LLMs and could reasonably be viewed as an early, incomplete AGI system.
contributions: A qualitative, psychology-style probing of an early GPT-4 on novel tasks across language, vision, coding, mathematics, tool use, theory of mind, explainability and discriminative tasks
An analysis of limitations tied to autoregressive next-word prediction (lack of planning, working memory, backtracking)
A discussion of societal influences and of definitions of and routes to AGI

method.summary: The authors prompted an early, non-multimodal version of GPT-4 during its development with natural-language prompts and compared it with ChatGPT and other models on hand-made tasks and a few benchmarks (HumanEval, LeetCode, GSM8K, MATH, MMMLU-STEM, TruthfulQA, TAB PII). Most evidence is qualitative examples; the paper states its approach is subjective and informal.
method.task: Open-ended capability probing of an LLM; small quantitative benchmark checks

datasets.name: LeetCode post-Oct-2022 set
datasets.source: leetcode.com problems posted after October 8th, 2022 (after GPT-4 pretraining period); graded by the official LeetCode online judge
datasets.preprocessing: problem text pasted into the prompt, model asked for a python function

datasets.name: GSM8K / MATH / MMMLU-STEM
datasets.preprocessing: model asked to write a template then steps then final answer; single-model accuracy (one try)

datasets.name: TruthfulQA
datasets.size: 816 questions across 38 categories (median 7, mean 21.5 per category)
datasets.preprocessing: preamble of Q/A pairs then the question; GPT-4 and GPT-3 each complete the answer

other.token_limit_mentioned: 8129 tokens (Appendix C.7: 'approaches its token limit of 8129')

other.note: Table 3 numbers appear to be reported from other work; the paper does not say so explicitly

inference.samples: Varies by experiment: 100 random samples per arithmetic setting (Sec 8.2); pass@1 and pass@5 on LeetCode; 5 runs per occupation in the bias experiment; HumanEval pass@1 zero-shot; unicorn drawing queried 3 times over a month
inference.prompting: Zero-shot natural-language prompts; step-by-step prompt for arithmetic (Sec 8.2); few-shot preamble for TruthfulQA generation; zero-shot instructions for PII and judge prompts

other.access: early access during OpenAI development; model changed during the experiments; final deployed model will give different results (footnote 1)

metrics.name: pass@k
metrics.definition: whether the model produces a correct solution in the first (k=1) or first five (k=5) attempts

metrics.name: single model accuracy
metrics.definition: percentage of questions answered correctly in one try

metrics.name: exact-match arithmetic accuracy
metrics.definition: percentage of 100 random expressions answered correctly

metrics.name: PII element count match
metrics.definition: whether the number of PII elements found equals ground truth, or misses 1, 2, or more than 2

metrics.name: Judge GPT-4 selection rate
metrics.definition: share of questions where GPT-4 as judge picks the GPT-4, GPT-3, neither or both answer as closer to the reference

eval.protocol: Mostly informal qualitative comparison; authors say the approach is subjective and may not satisfy rigorous scientific standards. Human check of the judge used two independent reviewers on a subset, no inter-rater agreement.

prompts.text:
What is the value of the following expression? 116 * 114 + 178 * 157 = ?
- Let’s think step by step to solve the expression, write down all the intermediate the steps, and only then produce the final solution.
Q: How many prime numbers are there between 150 and 250?
Q: First list the prime numbers between 150 and 250, and then output the size of this list.
I had a great experience with a <OCCUPATION>. Can you write a note recommending this <OCCUPATION> to a friend.

evidence.quote: As GPT-4 ’s development continued after our experiments, one should expect diﬀerent responses from the ﬁnal version of GPT-4.

results.claim: On 100 random a*b + c*d expressions with four numbers drawn from 0-9, early GPT-4 answers directly with only 58% accuracy.
results.setup: Early GPT-4, direct answer, four numbers uniform in 0-9, 100 random samples, no step-by-step instruction
results.quote: We tested the model with 100 random samples with the four numbers generated uniformly between 0 and 9, and obtain only 58% accuracy.

results.claim: The same direct-answer accuracy drops to 16% for numbers in 10-19 and 12% for 20-39, and to zero for 99-199.
results.setup: Early GPT-4, direct answer, numbers uniform in 10-19 (16%), 20-39 (12%)
results.quote: the accuracy drops to 16% and 12% respectively, and when the numbers are in the interval 99 and 199, the accuracy drops to zero
results.note: Sample count for these intervals is not stated (100 is given for the 0-9 case only).

results.claim: Asking for all intermediate steps raises accuracy to 100% for numbers in 1-40 and 90% for 1-200.
results.setup: Early GPT-4 with the 'Let's think step by step ... write down all the intermediate steps' prompt; numbers in 1-40 (100%) and 1-200 (90%)
results.quote: then the accuracy goes to 100% when the numbers are in the interval 1 −40 and to 90% for the interval 1 −200.
results.note: Baseline_value 16% is the direct-answer accuracy for 10-19 and is a different interval, not a matched control.

results.claim: Asked directly how many primes lie between 150 and 250, GPT-4 answers 13; asked to list them first and then count, it answers 18, which is correct.
results.quote: A: There are 13 prime numbers between 150 and 250.
results.note: Anecdote, one prompt, not a rate.

results.claim: On the 'modify exactly one integer' task, GPT-4 solves 32/100 for range [0,9] falling only to 18/100 for [50,100], which the authors read as a planning failure rather than a calculation failure.
results.setup: Early GPT-4, step-by-step plan prompt, 100 samples A*B+C*D=E per range
results.note: The text says 'randomly sample the integers B, D from [3,9] and C, D from [a,b]' (D appears twice).

results.claim: Zero-shot pass@1 on HumanEval: GPT-4 82%, text-davinci-003 65%, code-davinci-002 39%, CODEGEN-16B 30%.
results.setup: HumanEval 164 problems, zero-shot, early GPT-4; authors warn it may have memorised HumanEval
results.table: Table 1, row GPT-4, column Accuracy (82%); row text-davinci-003 65%
results.note: Paper says final GPT-4 will differ and defers to OpenAI's technical report.

results.claim: On 100 fresh LeetCode problems posted after Oct 8 2022, GPT-4 gets 38.0% pass@1 and 53.0% pass@5 overall versus 38.2% for LeetCode human users.
results.setup: 100 LeetCode problems post-dating GPT-4 pretraining, python function, official judge; baseline text-davinci-003 pass@1 19.0; human = LeetCode contest users who scored nonzero
results.table: Table 2, row GPT-4, column Overall k=1 (38.0) and k=5 (53.0); row Human (LeetCode users) Overall 38.2
results.note: Table 2 prints Human Medium 37.7 while Table 9 prints 38.7.

results.claim: LeetCode human accuracy by difficulty is 72.2% Easy, 38.7% Medium, 7.0% Hard, 38.2% overall.
results.setup: Derived from contest statistics of users who scored nonzero
results.table: Table 9, row Human Accuracy, column Overall
results.note: Table 2 prints Medium as 37.7, Table 9 as 38.7.

results.claim: Single-try accuracy on maths sets: GPT-4 87.1% GSM8K, 42.5% MATH, 82.7% MMMLU-STEM, versus text-davinci-003 61.3 / 23.5 / 54.2 and Minerva 58.8 / 33.6 / 63.9.
results.setup: MATH dataset, early GPT-4, prompt asks for solution template then steps then final answer
results.table: Table 3, row GPT-4, column MATH (42.5%); row text-davinci-003 23.5%
results.note: Authors call the improvement 'modest' and attribute most GPT-4 errors to arithmetic.

results.claim: In 100 manually inspected wrong MATH answers, 68% of GPT-4 errors are arithmetic mistakes, 10% misunderstanding, 22% wrong approach.
results.setup: Random selection of 100 wrong MATH answers by early GPT-4, manual inspection
results.table: Table 4, row Arithmetic mistakes (including counting), column Percentage of wrong solutions

results.claim: On MATH-style questions with numbers altered, GPT-4 gets 75.2% while text-davinci-003 gets 0.2%.
results.setup: Degree-3 polynomial question with random x values and p(1); number of variants not stated
results.quote: The results show that GPT-4 achieves an accuracy of 75.2%, while text-davinci-003 only has an accuracy of 0.2%.

results.claim: GPT-4 matches the ground-truth PII element count in 77.4% of 6764 TAB sentences versus 40.8% for Presidio, zero-shot.
results.setup: TAB subset, zero-shot prompt giving only PII categories; Presidio as baseline; counting task only
results.quote: GPT-4 is able to match the groundtruth 77.4% of the times, while it misses a single PII element ≈13% of the time.
results.table: Table 5, row GPT-4 column All 77.4%; row Presidio column All 40.8%
results.note: Authors concede evaluation is not exhaustive across PII forms.

results.claim: Judge GPT-4 picks the GPT-4 answer 87.76% of the time against GPT-3 on TruthfulQA, but humans agree only 50.8% of the time.
results.setup: TruthfulQA 816 questions; judge is GPT-4 itself picking between GPT-4 and GPT-3 answers; baseline_value is the human expert rate of picking the GPT-4 answer on a subset
results.quote: Judge GPT-4 picks the GPT-4-generated answer 87.76% of the time, the GPT-3-generated answer 11.01% of the time and neither answer 1.23 % of the time.
results.note: Human check on a subset (size not stated), two reviewers, no inter-rater agreement. 'There was a 50.8% overlap between the decisions made by Judge GPT-4 with humans'.

results.claim: In the bias experiment GPT-4 reference letters use 'he' with probability 0.98 for software engineer and 'she' 0.99 for nanny, tracking world occupation gender skew.
results.setup: Early (pre-alignment) GPT-4, 5 runs per occupation, first gendered word, probabilities collapsed into she/he/they groups
results.table: Table 7, row Nanny, column GPT-4 Pronoun Likelihoods (0.99 she)
results.note: Adding 'in an inclusive way' shifted the pronoun to they/their.

results.claim: Pseudo-code execution accuracy falls from 95% at 32 steps to 54% at 96 steps.
results.setup: Pseudo-code function g, one length-4 array fixed, other varied; steps = updates to array r; 100 samples
results.quote: the model still manages to keep track of the array r up to 54%
results.note: Paper says output nears 'its token limit of 8129'.

results.claim: On a simple algebra task GPT-4 accuracy drops from 98.1% at length 1 to 34.6% at length 5, versus text-davinci-003 51.5% to 1.0%.
results.setup: L in [5], a_i in {-1,1}, b_i, c_i in {-5..5}; sample count not stated
results.table: Table in App D.1, row GPT-4, column Length 5 (34.6%) and Length 1 (98.1%)
results.note: Table is unnumbered in the text.

results.claim: In LeetCode mock interviews the early GPT-4 scored 8.96/10, 8.69/10 and 10/10 across three rounds, beating 93%, 97% and 100% of users.
results.setup: LeetCode Interview Assessment platform, three rounds, 10 minutes total of 4.5 hours allotted
results.quote: According to LeetCode, in those three rounds respectively, (the early version of) GPT-4 achieves 8.96/10, 8.69/10, and 10/10 scores and beats 93%, 97%, and 100% of all users

results.claim: Preliminary multiple-choice tests gave about 80% on USMLE Steps 1-3 and above 70% on the Multistate Bar Exam.
results.setup: Multiple-choice component only, preliminary; details deferred to OpenAI report
results.quote: with an accuracy around 80% in each

results.claim: The authors say GPT-4's failures on planning stem from next-word prediction, which gives no scratchpad or backtracking, and separate incremental from discontinuous tasks.
results.setup: Interpretation of Section 8 examples; the paper also concedes it cannot separate RLHF effects from architectural ones

limits: All quantitative results are for an early, text-only version of GPT-4 and 'will be different on the final version'; numbers are 'for illustration purpose only' (Sec 3 disclaimer, footnote 1).
Method is 'somewhat subjective and informal' and 'may not satisfy the rigorous standards of scientific evaluation' (Sec 1.1); most evidence is hand-picked examples with no sample counts.
Possible contamination: authors assume GPT-4 may have seen benchmarks (knows BIG-bench canary GUID) and HumanEval, which motivates the LeetCode set.
Study is 'entirely phenomenological' and does not explain why or how (Sec 10.3).
Authors concede no clear separation between drawbacks from RLHF and those inherent to the architecture (Sec 10.2).
Judge GPT-4 agrees with humans only 50.8% of the time; human check had no inter-rater agreement and a subset of unstated size.
Training data, parameter count, compute and training recipe of GPT-4 are not given.
The AGI framing has since been disputed; the paper itself lists missing capabilities (calibration, memory, continual learning, planning).

terms.definition: tasks which can be solved in a gradual or continuous way, by adding one word or sentence at a time that constitutes progress in the direction of the solution
tasks where the content generation cannot be done in a gradual or continuous way, but instead requires a certain 'Eureka' idea that accounts for a discontinuous leap
systems that demonstrate broad capabilities of intelligence, including reasoning, planning, and the ability to learn from experience, and with these capabilities at or above human-level

ChatGPT described as a fine-tuned improved GPT-3; GPT-3 used in TruthfulQA comparison
Transformer architecture the LLMs are based on
